//: The URL->targetId wire contract, as DATA. Two independent implementations serialize this key - this client, and the backend that recomputes it before storing a vote - and a build in either one pins nothing about the other. So the vectors live here, in one machine-readable file, rather than as a table inside a test file that only one side can run: the client reads it through adapters/lockstep.test.ts, the backend reads the same file (pinned by commit) instead of keeping a second copy that drifts silently. Same arrangement as shared/__data__/emoji-categories.json, which the runtime and the build script both read.
//rules: urlDerivable[].url must derive targetId; the canonical URL that derivation emits must re-derive to the same id (idempotence); every variantUrls entry - another live surface of the SAME item - must converge on that id; every noTargetUrls entry must derive nothing. notUrlDerivable sites have no URL-only derivation at all, so neither side may invent one.

notUrlDerivable.why: the canonical id is GitLab's numeric project id, read from the page
photo and lazy-permalink identities are resolved from the DOM
